source_text: Ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἷς ὢν πλείονα τῇ ἐπινοίᾳ ἦν. καὶ τοῖς βλέπουσιν οὐχ ὁμοίως πᾶσιν ὁρώμενος. καὶ ὅτι μὲν τῇ ἐπινοίᾳ πλείονα ἦν, σαφὲς ἐκ τοῦ „ἐγώ εἰμι ἡ ὁδὸς καὶ ἡ ἀλήθεια καὶ ἡ ζωὴ“ καὶ τοῦ „ἐγώ εἰμι ὁ ἄρτος“ καὶ τοῦ „ἐγώ εἰμι ἡ θύρα“ καὶ ἄλλων μυρίων. ὅτι δὲ καὶ βλεπόμενος οὐχ ὡσαύτως τοῖς βλέπουσιν ἐφαίνετο. ἀλλ᾿ ὡς ἐχώρουν οἱ βλέποντες, σαφὲς ἔσται τοῖς ἐφιστᾶσι, διὰ τί μέλλων μεταμορφοῦσθαι ἐν τῷ ὑψηλῷ ὄρει οὐδὲ τοὺς ἀποστόλους πάντας παρείληφεν ἀλλὰ μόνους τὸν Πέτρον καὶ τὸν Ἰάκωβον καὶ τὸν Ἰωάννην. ὡς μόνους χωροῦντας τὴν τότε δόξαν αὐτοῦ θεωρῆσαι. δυναμένους δὲ καὶ τοὺς ὀφθέντας ἔν δόξῃ Μωϋσέα καὶ Ἠλίαν κατανοῆσαι καὶ ἀκοῦσαι συλλαλούντων αὐτῶν καὶ τῆς ἀπὸ τῆς νεφέλης οὐρανόθεν φωνῆς. ἐγὼ δ᾿ οἶμαι ὅτι καὶ πρὸ τοῦ ἀναβῆναι εἰς τὸ ὄρος. ἔνθα προσῆλθον αὐτῷ μόνοι οἱ μαθηταὶ καὶ ἐδίδασκεν αὐτοὺς τὰ περὶ τῶν μακαρισμῶν. ἡνίκα κάτω που ὢν τοῦ ὄρους „ὀψίας“ „γενομένης“ ἐθεράπευε τοὺς προσαχθέντας αὐτῷ. ἀπαλλάσσων πάσης νόσου καὶ πάσης μαλακίας. οὐχ ὁ αὐτὸς ἐφαίνετο τοῖς κάμνουσι καὶ δεομένοις αὐτοῦ θεραπεύοντος καὶ τοῖς διὰ τὸ ὑγιαίνειν συναναβῆναι αὐτῷ εἰς τὸ ὄρος δυνηθεῖσιν. ἀλλὰ καὶ εἴπερ κατ᾿ ἰδίαν τοῖς ἰδίοις μαθηταῖς ἐπέλυεν τὰς παραβολὰς. μετ᾿ ἐπικρύψεως τοῖς ἔξω ὄχλοις εἰρημένας. ὥσπερ ταῖς ἀκοαῖς ἦσαν κρείττους οἱ ἀκούοντες τῆς λύσεως τῶν παραβολῶν παρὰ τοὺς ἀκούοντας τῶν χωρὶς λύσεων παραβολῶν. οὕτως καὶ ταῖς ὄψεσι πάντως μὲν τῆς ψυχῆς. ἐγὼ δ᾿ ἡγοῦμαι ὅτι καὶ τοῦ σώματος. δηλοῖ δὲ μὴ τὸν αὐτὸν ἀεὶ φαίνεσθαι τὸ Ἰούδαν μέλλοντα αὐτὸν προδιδόναι εἰρηκέναι ὡς μὴ εἰδόσιν αὐτὸν τοῖς συναπερχομένοις αὐτῷ ὄχλοις· „ὃν ἐὰν φιλήσω. αὐτός ἐστι.“ τοιοῦτο δ᾿ οἶμαι καὶ αὐτὸν τὸν σωτῆρα ἐμφαίνειν διὰ τοῦ· „καθ᾿ ἡμέραν μεθ᾿ ὑμῶν ἤμην ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ διδάσκων. καὶ οὐκ ἐκρατήσατέ με.“ ὡς περὶ τηλικούτου οὖν φερόμενοι ἡμεῖς τοῦ Ἰησοῦ οὐ μόνον κατὰ τὴν ἔνδον καὶ ἀποκεκρυμμένην τοῖς πολλοῖς θειότητα ἀλλὰ καὶ κατὰ τὸ μεταμορφούμενον σῶμα. ὅτ᾿ ἐβούλετο καὶ οἷς ἐβούλετο. φαμὲν ὅτι τὸν μὲν μὴ ἀπεκδυσάμενον „τὰς ἀρχὰς καὶ τὰς ἐξουσίας“ Ἰησοῦν καὶ μηδέπω ἀποθανόντα „τῇ ἁμαρτίᾳ“ πάντες βλέπειν ἐχώρουν. τὸν δ᾿ ἀπεκδυσάμενον „τὰς ἀρχὰς καὶ τὰς ἐξουσίας“ καὶ μηκέτ᾿ ἔχοντά τι χωρητὸν ὁραθῆναι τοῖς πολλοῖς οὐχ οἶοί τε ἦσαν αὐτὸν βλέπειν οἱ πρότερον αὐτὸν ἰδόντες πάντες· ὅθεν φειδόμενος αὐτῶν οὐκ ἐφαίνετο πᾶσιν ἀναστὰς ἐκ νεκρῶν.
pass_a_gloss: Jesus, being one (εἷς), was more (πλείονα) in conception (ἐπίνοια), and was not seen alike by all those seeing. That he was more in conception is clear from ‘I am the way (ὁδός) and the truth (ἀλήθεια) and the life (ζωή)’ and ‘I am the bread (ἄρτος)’ and ‘I am the door (θύρα)’ and myriad others. That also being seen he did not appear the same to those seeing but as the seers had room (χωρέω), will be clear to those who attend (ἐφίστημι), why, being about to be transfigured (μεταμορφόω) on the high mountain, he did not take along (παραλαμβάνω) even all the apostles but only Peter and James and John, as alone having room to behold (θεωρέω) his glory (δόξα) then, and being able also to perceive (κατανοέω) Moses and Elijah seen in glory and to hear them conversing together (συλλαλέω) and the voice from the cloud from heaven (οὐρανόθεν). And I think that also before going up the mountain, where only the disciples came to him and he taught them the things about the beatitudes (μακαρισμοί), when being somewhere below the mountain, ‘evening’ ‘having come,’ he was healing (θεραπεύω) those brought to him, freeing them from every disease (νόσος) and every sickness (μαλακία), he did not appear the same to the sick and those needing him healing and to those who because of being healthy were able to go up the mountain with him. But also, if indeed privately (κατ᾿ ἰδίαν) to his own disciples he explained (ἐπιλύω) the parables (παραβολαί) spoken with concealment (ἐπίκρυψις) to the crowds outside, as in hearings those hearing the explanation (λύσις) of the parables were better (κρείττους) than those hearing the parables without explanations, so also in sights, entirely of the soul, but I hold also of the body. And it shows that he did not always appear the same, that Judas, about to betray (προδίδωμι) him, said, as to ones not knowing him, to the crowds going away with him: ‘Whomever I kiss (φιλέω), he is it.’ Such a thing I think the Saviour himself also indicates (ἐμφαίνω) through: ‘Daily I was with you in the temple (ἱερόν) teaching, and you did not seize (κρατέω) me.’ Being carried then (φέρομαι) with a view of Jesus as so great, not only according to the divinity (θειότης) within and hidden from the many but also according to the body being transfigured when he wished and to whom he wished, we say that the Jesus who had not stripped off (ἀπεκδύομαι) ‘the principalities (ἀρχαί) and the powers (ἐξουσίαι)’ and had not yet died ‘to sin (ἁμαρτία)’ all had room to see; but the one who had stripped off ‘the principalities and the powers’ and no longer had anything capable (χωρητόν) of being seen by the many, not all those who had seen him before were able to see; whence, sparing (φείδομαι) them, he did not appear to all having risen from the dead.
pass_b_english: Jesus, though one, was many in aspect; and he was not seen alike by all who saw him. That he was many in aspect is clear from “I am the way and the truth and the life” (John 14:6), and “I am the bread” (John 6:35), and “I am the door” (John 10:9), and countless other sayings. That even when seen he did not appear the same to all who saw him, but according to what each beholder could receive, will be clear to those who consider why, when he was about to be transfigured on the high mountain, he did not take even all the apostles, but only Peter and James and John (Matthew 17:1–2). For they alone could take in the sight of his glory at that time, and were able also to perceive Moses and Elijah, who appeared in glory (Luke 9:30–31), and to hear them talking together, and the voice from heaven out of the cloud (Matthew 17:5).

And I think that even before he went up the mountain, where only the disciples came to him and he taught them about the beatitudes (Matthew 5:1–12), when he was somewhere below the mountain and, “when evening had come” (Matthew 8:16), was healing those brought to him, freeing them from every disease and every sickness (Matthew 4:23), he did not appear the same to the sick who needed his healing as to those who, because they were healthy, were able to go up the mountain with him.

Moreover, since he privately explained to his own disciples the parables that had been spoken in a veiled way to the crowds outside (Mark 4:11, 34), then just as those who heard the explanation of the parables were superior in their hearing to those who heard the parables without explanations, so too were they superior in their sight: certainly the sight of the soul, and, I believe, of the body as well.

That he did not always appear the same is shown by what Judas said, when about to betray him, to the crowds who came out with him, as to men who did not know him: “Whomever I kiss, he is the one” (Matthew 26:48). I think the Saviour himself also indicates something of this in the words: “Day after day I was with you in the temple teaching, and you did not seize me” (Matthew 26:55; Mark 14:49).

Since, then, our view of Jesus is that he is so great, not only in the divinity within him, hidden from the many, but also in his body, which was transfigured when he wished and for those he wished, we say this: all were able to see Jesus while he had not yet “stripped off the principalities and the powers” (Colossians 2:15) and had not yet died “to sin” (Romans 6:10). But once he had stripped off “the principalities and the powers” and no longer had anything the many could take in by sight, not all who had seen him before were able to see him. Hence, sparing them, he did not appear to all when he had risen from the dead.

choices.why: χωρέω calque ‘had room to receive / behold’ replaced with ‘could receive’ / ‘could take in the sight of’; note updated.
διὰ τὸ ὑγιαίνειν made causal: ‘because they were healthy’.
John 14:6, 6:35, 10:9; Matthew 17:1–5, Luke 9:30–31; Matthew 5:1–12, 8:16, 4:23; Mark 4:11, 34; Matthew 26:48, 26:55, Mark 14:49; Colossians 2:15; Romans 6:10 checked against the wording.

translator_notes: ἐπίνοια is Origen’s term for the many titles or aspects under which the one Christ is conceived; rendered ‘aspect’. χωρέω (have room for, be able to receive) rendered ‘could receive’ / ‘could take in’ / ‘were able to’, avoiding the calque ‘had room’. ‘Seen in glory’ (ὀφθέντες ἐν δόξῃ) is Luke 9:31’s wording, hence the Luke citation; the voice from the cloud follows Matthew 17:5 (also Mark 9:7; Luke 9:35). ‘When evening had come’ and the healings echo Matthew 8:16, which in Matthew follows the Sermon on the Mount; Origen’s ‘before he went up’ is kept as the Greek has it. ‘Every disease and every sickness’ is the wording of Matthew 4:23 (also 9:35). ‘Privately to his own disciples he explained’ echoes Mark 4:34; ‘those outside’ Mark 4:11. Judas’s words match Matthew 26:48 (also Mark 14:44). The temple saying mixes Matthew 26:55 and Mark 14:49 (ἤμην follows Mark). Colossians 2:15 and Romans 6:10 supply the quoted phrases ‘stripped off the principalities and the powers’ and ‘died to sin’; Origen applies them to the risen Jesus.
